recentItems.title: Yemen’s education system strained by conflict and displacement
recentItems.description:
The conflict in Yemen has triggered a deepening displacement crisis, with the UN estimating that more than 320,000 people have been forced from their homes since August, nearly half of them children. UNICEF and the Yemeni Education Ministry estimate that 3.2 million children are currently out of class because of war or poverty, a figure that could rise dramatically if the fighting does not stop soon. 

Al Jazeera's Malik Traina reports.

recentItems.title: Who is Gadi Eizenkot, the former army chief chosen to form Israel’s government?
recentItems.description:
Gadi Eizenkot, a former Israeli army chief of staff, is one of the main challengers to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party. After retiring from the army in 2019, he entered the Knesset in 2022 and now leads the newly formed right-of-centre Yashar party. He opposes Palestinian statehood, supports retaining large illegal settlements and says Israel must maintain military and security control from the river to the sea.

Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh reports.

recentItems.title: Heritage, culture and crafts featured at Design Doha Biennale 2026
recentItems.description:
Qatar’s growing creative scene is drawing on traditional craftsmanship and contemporary design as the country pursues its ambition to build a knowledge-based economy. At Liwan, a Qatar Museums-operated creative and cultural hub housed in Qatar’s first girls’ school, designers say the building’s history continues to inspire their work. 

Al Jazeera's Cara Legg reports from Doha, Qatar.

recentItems.title: Brief: Tents flood in Gaza, will US blockade Iran's land borders? | The Take
recentItems.description:
This week: 394 days after the declaration of a ceasefire in Gaza,  Israel has killed at least 1,610 Palestinians there. Palestinians in Gaza face another winter without shelter. The US announced a plan to further blockade Iran. The process of forming a new Israeli government has begun.

Israel has killed at least 74,640 Palestinians in Gaza since October 7, 2023.

recentItems.title: Afghanistan’s Bamiyan restores heritage sites to draw foreign visitors
recentItems.description:
Restoration work is under way at heritage sites in central Afghanistan’s Bamiyan province, where ancient cave dwellings and the ruins of Shahr-e Gholghola face increasingly severe storm damage.

Officials say more than half a million tourists, mostly Afghans, visited Bamiyan in the past six months, a 50 percent increase from a year earlier. However, overseas visitors remain relatively few, with decades of conflict and Afghanistan’s international isolation deterring many foreign travellers. 

Al Jazeera's Rob McBride reports.

recentItems.title: Youth Olympics: Palestinian and refugee athletes compete ‘with or without a country’ in Dakar
recentItems.description:
At the Youth Olympics in Dakar, a swimmer from East Timor, independent for 24 years, greets a competitor whose homeland has been occupied for 59 years: 16-year-old Alma Shaat, representing Palestine. She says she is honoured, as people in Palestine won’t get the chance to compete at such a level. She tells any little girl in Gaza and Palestine to keep following her dream, as she does it for her people.

Six refugees unable to wear national kits compete under the colours of the refugee team in taekwondo, judo and athletics. Among them is 16-year-old sprinter Rachid, born in the Democratic Republic of Congo, who has spent most of his life in a displacement camp in Uganda. He wants to be remembered for his achievements on the track, and idolises Usain Bolt.

Al Jazeera’s Nicolas Haque reports from Dakar.
